transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I'm mostly here because HR at work and my sister have been on my case. They keep saying I've gotten too thin. I don't really see it like that, though. My suits just fit sharper, honestly. I guess my weight has kept dropping since my divorce, but... yeah. They told me I needed to come in.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I mean... I guess nobody really *wants* to gain weight, right? But... yeah, if I step on the scale after, say, a client dinner, or like a weekend trip to Miami, and it's even a pound higher... I don't know. I get this... panic, I guess. Like things are slipping out of control. I usually just figure out how to cut back the next day to fix it.
Do you think your current weight is normal?

Um... I don't know. I mean, I know everyone else is making a huge deal out of it. But... look, I still go jogging. I'm out working my territory every day, hitting my sales numbers. So... it just doesn't feel like some medical emergency to me. I'm functioning fine.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that feels excessive to you in a short period of time?
Um... no. Not really. I don't eat like that.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No. I've never... no, I don't do that.
Do you exercise to control your weight?
Um... no. I just... I run to clear my head. It's just a habit.
Do you think you look thin when you look in the mirror?

Um... no. Not really. I don't see thin. I just... I mean, if I'm getting ready for a client meeting, or a date... I usually just zero in on my stomach. Or my face. And if I think I look... soft, I guess... I just feel like people are going to see me as sloppy. Or weak. So... no.
Would you say that the fear of gaining weight is what mostly motivates you to control your eating?

I mean... I don't know if I'd call it fear. I just... I don't like it when the numbers go up. Like, if I have a client dinner, or... a weekend out in Miami... and the scale is even a pound higher after... I just get this... panic, I guess. It feels like I'm losing control. So I just... I start planning how to cut back the next day. I just want to keep things handled, that's all.
Do you think your weight or body shape affects how much you eat?
I don't know. I guess... maybe? I just try to eat what I need to. I don't really think about it like that.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as overweight even if others say you are underweight?

I mean... like I was saying earlier... I don't really look at it like that. I don't know about the word 'overweight.' I just... when I'm checking the mirror before a meeting or a date or something... I just see my stomach. Or my face. And if it looks soft... I just know people are going to think I'm sloppy. Or weak. So... that's just what I see.
When you think about your body, do you think it is larger than it actually is?
I... I don't know. I don't really think about it being larger or smaller. I just... see what I see.
Do you think your weight is lower than what other people think it is?
I don't really know what other people think. I don't ask them. I just... I know what the scale says. I don't really worry about if it's lower or higher than what someone else is guessing.
Do you think your body shape or weight is the same as how others see it?
I... I really couldn't tell you. I don't ask people how they see my shape. It's just... not something I talk about with anybody. So I don't know if it matches or not.
When you look at yourself, do you think you appear fat even when others tell you that you are too thin?

I... I don't really pay attention to what people say about me being thin. I just... when I look in the mirror, like before a client meeting or a date, I tend to zero in on my stomach and my face. If I think I look soft... I just feel like people are going to see me as sloppy. Or weak. That's really it.
Do you think there's a difference between how you see your body and how it actually looks?
I don't... I don't think so. The mirror just shows what's there. I mean, I'm just looking at the reality of it. I don't think my eyes are playing tricks on me or anything.
Do you think your body appears normal to you when you look in the mirror?
I don't... I'm not really sure what you mean by normal. It's just... my body. I just see what's there in the mirror. I don't really think about it in terms of being normal or not.
Do you think your body shape is different from what others see when they look at you?
I... I have no idea. I can't really speak for what other people see. I just assume we're looking at the same thing.
Do you think your body shape is different from how it actually is?
I... I don't think so. I feel like we kind of just went over this. It's... it's just my body. I don't think I'm seeing it differently than how it actually is.
Do you think you would be upset if you gained a small amount of weight?

I guess... yeah, it bothers me. If I have a client dinner or, you know, go away for a weekend and the scale is even a pound higher... I just get this sort of panic. Like things are slipping. Then I just figure out how to cut back the next day to fix it.
Do you think your body shape is the same as it appears in pictures of you?
I don't really look at pictures of myself. If I do, I guess it looks like me. I don't know.
